transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I don’t think I’m getting the truth about my father’s death. People say the hospital records and donation emails all match up, but when I look at the timestamps, the missing attachments, and how some people in the community avoid my questions... it seems clear someone is hiding something.
Have you heard any voices or sounds when there was no one around to make them?
No, I haven’t heard voices or sounds that weren’t actually there.
Outside of this situation with your father, do you often find it hard to trust the intentions of people around you?
Not generally, no. I mean, I’m cautious like anyone, but I don’t usually assume people are out to mislead me. This is different because of the things I’ve noticed around my father’s case.
Is there any doubt in your mind that people are intentionally hiding something about your father's death?

No, I don’t really have doubt. I know people say the records and donation emails line up, but the timestamps, the missing attachments, and the way certain people avoid answering me... it’s clear someone is withholding what actually happened to my father.
How long have you felt that people are hiding the truth about what happened to your father?
About nine months now. It started after my father died, when I began going through his records and messages.

The delusion has persisted for approximately nine months, exceeding the three-month duration threshold for ICD-10 F22 (Persistent delusional disorder). There are no auditory hallucinations, cognitive impairments, or pervasive lifelong paranoid traits outside of this specific theme.
